title: Absolute algebraic dualizing complexes for proper schemes over fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $a$ be a right adjoint of $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_C)\to D(k)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Put $K=a(k[0])$. Then $K$ is an absolute algebraic dualizing complex on $C$: it has bounded coherent cohomology, every stalk $K_x$ is an algebraic dualizing complex over the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{C,x}$, that is, $K_x$ has finite injective dimension over $\mathcal O_{C,x}$, and the scalar map $\mathcal O_{C,x}\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{C,x}}(K_x,K_x)$ is an isomorphism in the derived category. Finite injective dimension for a complex means that it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective modules; coherent modules are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. The assertion allows arbitrary dimension, disconnected schemes and arbitrary fields.

source.place: Tag 0AA3 (lemma-shriek-dualizing), applied to the dualizing complex k[0] on Spec k; Tag 0AWI (example-proper-over-local) and the immediately following example-equidimensional-over-field identify this with the proper adjoint dualizing complex.

proof.text: Properness gives finite type, hence a finite affine cover $C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with every $B_i$ a finite-type $k$-algebra. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$. The finite-type Noetherian-algebra theorem makes every $B_i$ Noetherian, and the finite-presentation theorem gives finite polynomial presentations over $k$. Thus $C$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is locally of finite presentation. It is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by separatedness, so is of finite presentation. Every morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by the cited field-flatness lemma.

source.place: Tag 0AA3, lemma-shriek-dualizing, hypotheses; algebra.tex Tags 00FN and 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-permanence and lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Apply the proper-flat polynomial-model theorem to $f$. It gives a right adjoint $f^!$ and $K_f=f^!\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$. The affine derived equivalence identifies $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ with $k[0]$ and the target derived category with $D(k)$. Uniqueness of right adjoints therefore identifies the given $a$ with $f^!$ and $K$ with $K_f$. For each chosen affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, choose generators and a surjection $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$. The same theorem identifies $K|_U$ in $D(B)$ with $L_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/k})[n]$, with the coinduced $B$-action.

source.place: Tag 0BV2, remark-local-calculation-shriek; Tag 0E4P, remark-relative-dualizing-complex-bis; proper adjoint identification.

proof.text: The polynomial regularity theorem makes $P$ Noetherian and $A=P_{\mathfrak q}$ a regular local ring for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset P$. The regular-local injective-resolution theorem gives a bounded injective representative of $A[0]$. Its only cohomology module is the cyclic module $A$. Since $A$ is free of rank one over itself, the projective-resolution calculation of derived Hom gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A,A)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(A,A)[0]\cong A[0]$ by evaluation at $1$; the scalar map is the inverse of evaluation. Thus $A[0]$ has exactly the three properties required of the input to finite-map dualizing transfer. This establishes those properties locally, without an assertion about a bounded injective model over the nonlocal ring $P$.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective; algebra.tex Tag 00OQ, proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring.

proof.text: The polynomial differential basis gives $\Omega^1_{P/k}=\bigoplus_{j=1}^nP\,dt_j$. Alternating multilinearity identifies $\Omega^n_{P/k}$ with $P$: send $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$ to $1$, and on arbitrary vectors use their coefficient determinant. Expansion expresses every wedge as this determinant times the displayed generator, proving these maps inverse; for $n=0$ use $\bigwedge^0P^0=P$. Set $M_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,P)$ with its coinduced $B$-action. Substituting the differential-basis isomorphism in step 2 gives $L_B\cong M_B[n]$ in $D(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0BV2, remark-local-calculation-shriek, top differential module; algebra.tex polynomial differential basis.

proof.text: For any ring $T$, if a complex $N$ has bounded finitely generated cohomology, a bounded injective representative, and an invertible scalar map $T\to R\operatorname{Hom}_T(N,N)$, then $N[n]$ has the same properties. Shift its bounded injective representative; its cohomology becomes $H^{j+n}(N)$. Shifting both Hom arguments cancels in $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(N[n],N[n])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_T(N,N)$. The cancellation sends $t\,\mathrm{id}_{N[n]}$ to $t\,\mathrm{id}_N$, so identifies the scalar maps. We will apply this elementary argument to the local complexes constructed in step 10; no such properties of $M_B$ over the unlocalized ring $B$ are assumed here.

source.place: Tag 0A7B, definition-dualizing, shift invariance by the three displayed conditions.

proof.text: Since $B$ is a quotient of the Noetherian ring $P$, it is cyclic as a $P$-module. The finite-free resolution theorem supplies an exact augmented resolution $F_\bullet\to B$ with every $F_i$ finite free; it need not terminate. Regard it as a bounded-above projective cochain resolution of $B[0]$. The projective derived-Hom calculation represents $M_B$, after forgetting its $B$-action, by $\operatorname{Hom}_P(F_\bullet,P)$. Its terms are finite free and occur only in nonnegative cohomological degrees. The Noetherian submodule theorem makes its cycles finitely generated; the cohomology, a quotient of the cycles, is finitely generated over $P$. It is therefore finitely generated over $B$ as well: for the coinduced action a lift in $P$ of $b\in B$ acts as $b$, and the same finite generators work. Also $H^j(M_B)=0$ for $j<0$.

source.place: Tags 00LP, lemma-resolution-by-finite-free (2), and 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective.

proof.text: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak M\subset P$, localization $P\to P_{\mathfrak M}$ is flat. Apply the flat coherent derived-Hom base-change statement with $C=B[0]$ and $Z=P[0]$; both have bounded finite cohomology over the Noetherian ring $P$. It identifies $(M_B)_{\mathfrak M}$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_{P_{\mathfrak M}}(B\otimes_PP_{\mathfrak M},P_{\mathfrak M})$. The local ring $P_{\mathfrak M}$ is regular by step 3 and has dimension $n$ by the maximal-localization dimension theorem. Its global dimension is at most $n$, so a projective resolution of length $n$ and the projective derived-Hom calculation give zero cohomology in degrees $j>n$. Flat localization commutes with cohomology. A module zero at all maximal localizations is zero: a nonzero element has a proper annihilator, contained in a maximal ideal, and cannot vanish there by the fraction criterion. Consequently $H^j(M_B)=0$ for $j>n$. Together with step 6 and the shift in step 4, this gives finite cohomology for $L_B$, supported in $[-n,0]$.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom (3); algebra.tex Tags 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (1), 00OP, lemma-dim-affine-space, and 00O7, proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim; projective calculation Tag 0A66.

proof.text: The affine equivalence of step 2 is induced by termwise associated sheaf, so the derived tilde-cohomology comparison gives $H^j(K)|_{U_i}\cong\widetilde{H^j(L_{B_i})}$. The finite-type affine-module criterion makes these quasi-coherent sheaves of finite type; since $U_i$ is locally Noetherian, the coherent/finite-type criterion makes them coherent. Coherence is local by its definition, so $H^j(K)$ is coherent on $C$. Step 7 supplies bounds $a_i=-n_i\le b_i=0$ for the cohomology of $L_{B_i}$. For nonempty $C$, the finite cover gives integers $a=\min_i a_i$, $b=\max_i b_i$; the displayed cohomology identifications imply $H^j(K)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, since a sheaf zero on an open cover is zero. Thus $K$ has bounded coherent cohomology. If $C$ is empty, its module category and its derived category have only the zero object, so the conclusion holds with bounds $[0,0]$.

source.place: Tag 0AA3, lemma-shriek-dualizing, affine locality; perfect.tex Tag 06Z0, lemma-affine-compare-bounded; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian.

proof.text:
For $x\in U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be its prime and $\mathfrak q\subset P$ its inverse image. The affine stalk-ring formula identifies $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ with $B_{\mathfrak p}$. Taking termwise associated sheaves of a complex representing $L_B$, the tilde-stalk formula and exactness of stalks identify $K_x\cong(L_B)_{\mathfrak p}$ in $D(B_{\mathfrak p})$. Put $A=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $D=B_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $B\otimes_PA=D$: the images of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$ are exactly $B\setminus\mathfrak p$, since $P\to B$ is surjective. The flat localization and coherent derived-Hom base-change statements, again applied to $C=B[0]$, $Z=P[0]$, give
$$(M_B)_{\mathfrak p}\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,A).$$
The canonical comparison is $D$-linear: coefficient localization respects $(b\varphi)(y)=\varphi(by)$, the action defining coinduction on both sides. Its underlying $A$-linear map is the base-change isomorphism, hence it is an isomorphism in $D(D)$ as well, since forgetting scalars detects zero cohomology of its cone. With step 4 this identifies $K_x$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,A)[n]$ as a derived $D$-object.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom (3); schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (6),(7); algebra.tex Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (1).

proof.text: The localized quotient $A=P_{\mathfrak q}\to D=B_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective, so $D$ is generated by $1$ as an $A$-module. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by step 3 and so is its quotient $D$ (ideals of $D$ lift to ideals of $A$). Apply finite-map dualizing transfer with the complex $A[0]$: finite cohomology, the bounded injective model and the scalar isomorphism were all verified in step 3. Its conclusion gives finite cohomology, a bounded injective representative and the scalar homothety isomorphism for $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,A)$ as a $D$-complex. Apply step 5 to its shift by $[n]$, and the derived identification of step 9. Thus $K_x$ has the asserted bounded injective representative and scalar homothety isomorphism over $D\cong\mathcal O_{C,x}$. Step 8 supplies the global bounded coherent cohomology. No equidimensionality, connectedness or perfection hypothesis was used.
